facts.fact: The ICT ministry's Digital Uganda Vision states that, under the NBI/EGI project, the Government through the ministry has provided connectivity to ministries, departments and agencies and to Local Governments by laying optical fibre across all major towns; no date is given for the statement, so the document's published date is used.
facts.system: National Backbone Infrastructure and e-Government Infrastructure (NBI/EGI)

facts.fact: The Vision's targets table gives the percentage of district headquarters connected to the NBI as 44% at its 2020 baseline, with targets of 70% for 2025, 90% for 2030 and 100% for 2040; no numerator or denominator is given, and the figure is the ICT ministry's.

The Vision states that under last-mile connectivity 575 of 700 planned sites had so far been connected, across 52 major districts, and that phase 4 brought connected MDAs to 603; it does not say how many of the sites are local government offices, and gives no date, so the published date is used.

The Vision states that the connectivity to MDAs and Local Governments under the NBI/EGI project was provided by the Government through the Ministry of ICT and National Guidance; no date is given, so the published date is used.
facts.system: National Backbone Infrastructure and e-Government Infrastructure (NBI/EGI)

facts.fact: The Digital Uganda Vision, adopted in September 2022 and running to 2040, sets as outcomes 100% of district headquarters connected to the national broadband infrastructure and 100% connectivity for all government institutions, both central and local governments, with interim targets of 50% for 2025 and 75% for 2030 on the second.
